summary: Claus Oetke (1947–2019) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served at Hamburg, held deputation professorships at Kiel and Vienna, and led Stockholm University's Indology department.

Claus Vogel (1933–2012) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He earned his PhD and completed his habilitation at the University of Marburg, also studying at Deccan College. He held posts at Marburg and Göttingen, and was an Ordinarius at Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She has held posts at the University of Canterbury as an Associate Professor in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.

Clemens a Jesu (1731–1782) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Urban College (~1750–1756). He served in the Archdiocese of Verapoly (~1758–1782) and became General Vicar of the Malabar Mission in 1774.

Clements Markham (1830–1916) worked in history, archaeology, and Tibetology after studying at Cheam School and Westminster School. He served as Secretary and President of both the Royal Geographical Society and the Hakluyt Society, and was Assistant Secretary at the India Office.
Clinton B. Seely (1936–2021) was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Chicago, where he served as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Clyde Kluckhohn (1905–1960) studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. His main academic posts were at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat (1921–2007) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Walther Schubring, Louis Renou, and Jules Bloch. She held posts at the CNRS, the University of Lyon, the Sorbonne, and was Director of the Institut de Civilisation Indienne.

Colette Sciberras is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.

Colin Mackenzie (1754–1821) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Dollar Academy. He served as an engineer in the Madras Engineer Group, Surveyor-General of Madras, and Surveyor General at the Survey of India (1810–1815).
Colin Turnbull (1924–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1949), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her PhD at Columbia University and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities. In 1985, she took up a professorship at the University of Washington.
Congjun Long works in computational linguistics and Tibetology and has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Conor Roddy is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin under Kathleen Higgins, having also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.
Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Leipzig and Berlin. He held posts at the universities of Leipzig, Tübingen, Zurich, Jena, and Munich.
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University from ~1927 to 1934 and served on the faculty at Columbia University from ~1946 to 1979.

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College and Emory University (PhD), and has held posts at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, Smith College, and Lawrence University.
Constance Powell Chin is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies who earned a master's degree at San Jose State University and studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constant Chounavel (1825–1923) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Major Seminary of Saint-Dié (~1845–1849). He served in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Jaffna (1852–1883) and was a pastor at St. Lucia's Cathedral.
